I was just dumbfounded. Is this really that annoying?

reviews.author: Akongi Restaurant Tour
reviews.text:
☆Pyongyang Naengmyeon: 13,000 won
☆1 dumpling: 2,000 won

The place to introduce today is [Onraeng], a hot Pyeongyang cold noodle restaurant located in Mapo-gu, Seoul.

✔️I visited Onraeng because an acquaintance in Seoul said it was one of the hottest Pyeonnaeng restaurants in 2025.

I had lunch earlier and was about to have a snack when I checked around 14:30 and it said it was closing, so this time I went to Busan for the open run. Thankfully, the owner of Dongria made a reservation for the open run in advance that day, so we went in together after having a cup of coffee at the cafe next door. (Thanks to the owner Dongria again)

Even before going inside, there seemed to be a lot of people waiting and the turnover rate was good.

✡️Pyongyang Naengmyeon
Appetizing cold noodles, meat, and eggs are placed in a large brass bowl, and the bowl is complete when you pour in the cool broth.

Once you sip the broth into your mouth, you get the meaty, nutty, and umami flavor, but the strong salinity felt somewhat artificial, and the salty taste lingered in your mouth for a long time.

The meat served as a garnish was soft and had the right amount of flavor, and the noodles were made upon ordering, so the texture of the noodles was also good, perhaps due to the high buckwheat content.

(Usually, Pyeongnaeng restaurants have a good jinhyang meat flavor and smoothness, but this place has a strong salt content, so people who don't normally eat Pyeongnaeng may like the Onnaeng Pyeongnaeng here.)

Maybe that's why there were a lot of young people waiting, and I think Pyeongnaeng was created to be able to be enjoyed by a wider range of age groups than the existing Pyeongnaeng.

✡️Dumplings
Usually, the skin of Pyeonnaengjip dumplings is thick, but the skin here is thin and the filling is full of tofu and meat, so it is delicious and the advantage is that you can order it as a single piece.

✔️Address: Onraeng, 1st floor, 33 Seongmisan-ro, Mapo-gu, Seoul
✔️Contact: Not registered
✔️Business hours: 11:30~16:00
✔️Parking facilities: None

1. Closed every Monday.
2. Last order is at 15:30, but on weekends it may close before then (note that on weekends, it may sell out during business hours).
3. Pyeongyang Naengmyeon had a meaty, nutty, and savory flavor, but the strong saltiness felt somewhat artificial. The salty taste lingered in the mouth for a long time, and the meat served as a topping was soft and had the right amount of meaty flavor. The noodles were made upon ordering, perhaps because of the high buckwheat content, but the curly noodles were also good.
4. The dumplings are delicious because they are thin and filling, and I like the young radish kimchi served as a side dish.
5. If the existing Pyeongnaeng has a larger fan base than the popular one, Onnaeng is a popular summer food that even young people can easily enjoy.
6. There was some talk that it was unfriendly, but I didn't feel that on the day I went.
7. Please note that excessive waiting can detract from the taste (waiting can be done by waiting on the catch table).

Overall evaluation: 《Onraeng, located in Seongsan-dong, Mapo-gu, Seoul, has become famous as a local restaurant.

Whenever I go to Seoul, I keep eating Pyeonnaeng as a snack, and I think Onnaeng is a place that has modified the limitations of the existing Pyeonnaeng to a popular location.

What I felt as I continued to visit the Pyeongnaeng restaurants was that each one had their own unique characteristics, which was nice, and this Pyeongnaeng restaurant also had its own unique personality, so it was a day where I could experience many things. 》

reviews.author: BONG
reviews.text:
Separated hot/cold menu on/raeng
Basically, the broth itself is meat broth, and it focuses on meat broth-based dishes such as dumplings or Pyongyang cold noodles.

Reservations can be made through Catch Table. There is a Catch Table machine on the wall right in front of the store, but the space to make a reservation and wait is a bit small and the surrounding environment is not good.

The interior consists of only tatami-shaped standing tables and there appear to be about 12 chairs.

It is about a 10-minute walk from Mangwon Station, and there are many cafes nearby, and it is a place where many people visit churches, cathedrals, and hiking/traveling around Seongsan Mountain.

I chose the Pyongyang Naengmyeon menu, and although the size of the bowl or the amount of noodles didn't seem very large or spacious, the noodles filled with buckwheat were quite attractive and the chewy texture was good.

The soup has a strong meaty flavor and is seasoned rather than plain, so it is easy to eat even for people who do not enjoy Pyongyang naengmyeon. Even if it's just cold noodles, it's not too far off. Instead, the price is Pyongyang Naengmyeon.

When it's cold, gomtang menu items are also sold in large quantities.

reviews.text:
The combination of Pyongyang cold noodles and dumplings is good.
It's clean but full of flavor, so it suddenly comes to mind.

I especially like the dumplings because they are very clean.
These were not dumplings with various seasonings including minced garlic, but very neatly seasoned tofu/pork/bean sprout dumplings. The seasoning was not salty or bland, but just enough to bring out the flavor of the dumplings themselves.

Pyongyang naengmyeon was also delicious. I liked the subtle meaty flavor, as if it were boring, and the noodles were neither too thin nor too thick. I don't like chewy noodles, but this one was reasonably chewy and soft.
Because salt-pickled cucumbers were included, the soup had a slightly cool/refreshing feel to it, and the toppings were sliced ​​thickly so there was no shortage of them.

My friend said that the gomtang (gomtang) was delicious and all the other menu items were delicious, so I'll have to try something different next time.

reviews.text:
Pyongyang Naengmyeon is easily accessible.

A Pyongyang cold noodle restaurant in an unexpected location near Sangam-dong.
There is a head office in Ilsan and it seems to be a branch.

Compared to the general Uijeongbu and Jangchung-dong strains, the liver is clearer.
There are a lot of shapes and quantities available without any likes or dislikes, so please be mindful when ordering.

On the other hand, the dumplings are very soft and the meat is okay.

Pyongyang Naengmyeon appears to be functioning as an everyday restaurant, as several local residents come out wearing slippers and eat alone.

It's not far away, but you won't regret stopping by when you're nearby.

Recommended menu: Pyongyang Naengmyeon

reviews.author: Kai Lee
reviews.text:
Gajwa Station Naengmyeon Restaurant Daedonggwan
The Seoul branch of Daedonggwan, the best Pyeongyang cold noodle restaurant in Ilsan, opened in 2009. It has the distinction of being located in Seongsan, which is relatively far away from Mapo-gu, the battleground for Pyongyang naengmyeon.
Pyongyang Naengmyeon had good broth and the noodles, which were made on the same day using pure buckwheat, were the best. As for the side dish, the red cabbage kimchi from North Korea was really delicious, and the mung bean pancake was a bit disappointing considering the price.

reviews.text: I went there with high expectations because it was a Pyongyang naengmyeon specialty restaurant, but unexpectedly, the Pyongyang naengmyeon was not as tasty by my standards compared to other restaurants like Eulmil and Nampo. However, the bibim naengmyeon was delicious, and the amazing thing about this restaurant was the beef small table, which gave me a deep taste of boiled pork that I had never tasted anywhere else. Next time, I will have to come to eat pork. And when I ate the galbitang, I felt that it tasted really boring, but when I checked it with Libre, I saw that my blood sugar level barely rose, so I was sure that it tasted like it had almost no chemical seasoning. This is a healthy rib soup recommended for elderly people. So I give it 5 stars.

I ordered red soup rice noodles, and it was good because it wasn't too spicy, clean, and not very spicy. The side dishes that came with it were also delicious.
The inside of the store is clean and the food is served neatly. Even the water is barley tea. It is evident that careful attention was paid to every detail. It would be nice to have a light meal nearby.

I was drawn to the Bichon Frize sticker outside the store. (Later I found out that the owner, Tenya, said it was only open on weekends.)

There was no English menu, but I was able to translate without problem using the Papago app. I ordered beef rice noodles, and it tasted like tomatoes and was spicy, but the spiciness was okay. It was my first time trying Korean pho, and the texture was similar to Phnom Penh pho in Vietnam. The beef slices were tender and flavorful.

The interior is decorated with hipster inspiration, and there are Zen-style flower trees inside. The music adds to the overall atmosphere.

The service was great. I think the dining experience would have been much better and more memorable if I had met the owner in person.

I ordered spicy tonkotsu ramen.
The noodles had a green wheat taste, as if they were not salty, and the overflowing cold bean sprouts were crunchy until the end of the meal.
There were two thin, small pieces of chashu that appeared to be about 4mm thick, and they were cold as if they had just been taken out of the refrigerator. (You can think of it as cold and shabby cold meat)
The egg was just half an egg boiled in water. He was cold too.
The only thing worth eating was the soup, which had an obvious taste.

I didn't even know that ramen like this existed in this world. Even for a low-priced Japanese restaurant, isn't that too much? It's not cheap either. If you add just 1,000 won more, you can eat spicy ramen that you won't regret at a famous place nearby. When you see so many things left behind, you ask me why I left them behind. Do you really not know? I think reflection is necessary.

(Hygiene and friendliness were not bad, so I raised it from 1 to 2.)
